Then we have the centre band, which as previously stated, is the same as if you had placed a 20 SMA on your chart (with 20, 2.0 settings). I am using this centre band as a potential filter for both entry into a trade and also as a potential warning signal to take some action if already in a trade, as it can be used for both trade entry and trade management purposes.

As the MACD Platinum is considered to be an oscillator type indicator, it can also be used to determine potential divergences with price, and it can also be used as an early warning signal for some trade management. This will all be covered later in the book with some examples.

To give you an example of this, say I am trading the High Probability trading system from one of my earlier books on the Daily charts. A new trade signal presents, which I then take at market with my full trade position size, with a risk percentage based on my analysis of the strength of that trade signal. I then set a stop loss on that trade and walk away from the chart. I do not set a profit target. I will then look at that same chart approximately 24hrs later and make any necessary adjustments. I discussed the use of divergence to assist with trade entries, but it can also be used for trade management, or at least give you a reason to tighten things up on a trade. For example, you may be in a buy trade that has been going nicely in your favour, but as price continues upwards, you may observe that the MACD Platinum is heading down at the same time, which is potentially setting up for regular bearish divergence. This is like an early warning signal, where it may be smart to consider moving your stop up on the buy trade and locking in some profit. And like I have said many times before, the higher the time frame you trade, the more time you have to look at the charts and make these decisions, where there is little pressure on you to do so. Take your time on each chart and consider all the options.
